runtime_assets: Generated MP3 files and a text-to-file catalog only. No source/reference recordings, service endpoint, model weights, profile path or dependency on VoiceStudio at runtime.
postprocessing: Per-clip constant gain toward -20 dBFS non-silent RMS (-50 dBFS block threshold), capped at -2 dBFS decoded-MP3 peak. Mono 24 kHz, 64 kbit/s MP3; no dynamic compression, pitch shift or time stretch in the asset conversion.

scope.documents: DocSpec.transcript paragraphs displayed by UI.document, and a separate reading of static DocSpec.page paragraphs. No titles. Page-only pencil prefixes and pure separator lines are removed identically in runtime and extraction.
scope.conversations: Existing Panels.talk lines retained. Visible reply and question prose is also included in narrative descriptions; button-choice labels remain excluded.
scope.radio: Original broadcast and CB playback is unchanged. Dedicated core/radio.ts, story/tripRadio.ts and core/cb.ts are not extracted. Quoted/captioned narrative text in chapter/event files can be read manually as descriptions.
scope.telephone: Canonical literal PHONE_CALLS cue.text except aside, and PHONE_TEXTS from src/core/phoneScripts.ts. Exact speech only; actor labels, quotation marks and the unsaid player aside are excluded. 24 phone texts reuse 15 existing clips and add nine from Ward/Nora in chapters 2 and 3.
scope.telephone_manuscript: production/kinski/telefonmanus.md: all 24 exact authored speech lines by scene and actor, with the unsaid chapter 2 player aside explicitly marked silent.
scope.descriptions: Displayed narrative examination, toast and note text; document description and paper paragraphs; panel instructions, questions and replies; case-board evidence, hints and findings; notebook tasks, notes, kit/person names, states, roles and notes; album captions and place/time metadata; map descriptions; chapter recaps. Exact static variants and source fragments only. UI button labels, developer menu, credits and broadcast radio scripts are excluded.
scope.freeze_note: Inventory frozen after concrete selector and dynamic resolver checks. Further additions require an actual rendered narrative text coverage gap.

dynamic_policy: No blanket exclusion for dynamic documents. Runtime first uses exact whole-text clips, then only a complete sequence of exact fragments and spoken numeric/identifier components. Any unknown word makes the whole requested block unavailable. No silent omission or unrestricted word synthesis.

qa.encoding: Every file ffprobe checked as mono 24000 Hz MP3 and decoded again for PCM energy, peak, positive duration and hash/manifest coverage.

asr.interpretation: Long samples retain their sentences, with ASR differences around IDs, homophones, number spelling and WASD. Zero is exact; twenty is written 20. Standalone six was recognized as Fix; the actual concatenated number-bank context was recognized as Zero, twenty, six. The short S was omitted by ASR. No human listening or speaker-similarity check is implied.

library_reference: prosjektbibliotek/OFFENTLIG_INVENTAR.md entry for debpalash/VoiceStudio. Existing installed local API and profile reused; no new model or service installed.
segmentation: Full normalized text first. Documents and plain description data split at blank paragraphs; page-only pencil markers and separator lines are removed. Narrative descriptions include displayed toast/note, examine, panel prose, board facts/hints, notebook names/roles/state/notes, album captions, map prose and chapter recaps. Finite branches are literal variants. Runtime templates retain every static fragment, resolved as a complete sequence with cardinal/decimal/clock words and strict identifier letters. No skipping unknown words. Telephone uses exact PHONE_CALLS speech except aside and PHONE_TEXTS. Button labels, development menu, credits and broadcast radio scripts are excluded.

pronunciation_policy: Catalog text and IDs remain exact. Numeric lexemes use capitalized sentence punctuation. Letter names use explicit pronunciations; A/H/X use the original letter with an exclamation mark after silent phonetic takes. The source abbreviation el is expanded to Elevation. Each different synthesis text has its own cache identity.
